description.text:
The first Pokémon Trading Card Game set in English, released by Wizards of the Coast on 9 January 1999: 102 cards, the English edition of the Japanese set of 20 October 1996. Its Pokémon all come from Kanto, and several evolution lines stop short because their last stages came in later sets. It was sold in booster packs, four theme decks (Blackout, Brushfire, Overgrowth and Zap!) and a two-player starter set, gave the game its first Special Energy, Double Colorless Energy, and is the only set printed with no set symbol.

Wizards kept printing Base Set until about the middle of 2000, after Team Rocket was out, and collectors tell its prints apart. The first carries a 1st Edition stamp. The next, without the stamp, lacks the shadow around the picture and has brighter colors and a thinner font, and is known as shadowless; the unlimited print adds the shadow. Both early prints were smaller runs than unlimited. The last, printed in 2000, has a 1999-2000 copyright line; its holos are known only from the copies printed in the United Kingdom and sold across Europe, so collectors call it the UK print or Base Set 2000.

description.text:
A test print of the Base Set holo in a holofoil pattern never used on any released Pokémon card. Collectors call it "disco", CGC's name for it, since it has no official one. Apart from the foil the card follows the Shadowless print, with no 1st Edition stamp, but some design elements are missing. One of the two or three known uncut sheets has a pressman's sign-off dated January 21, 1999, twelve days after Base Set came out, and uses the later Unlimited sheet layout, so it wasn't a prototype for Base Set; CGC suggests Wizards of the Coast was trying foils for later print runs or sets. description.text:
Base Set's Machamp wasn't in booster packs. Each 2-Player Starter Set held one beside its two 30-card half decks, as the set's only Stage 2 Pokémon: it joins when the halves are put together, and one card is taken out to make a 60-card deck. Every copy sold carries the 1st Edition stamp, through all the starter set's later printings, so there is no Unlimited Machamp. The only Base Set Machamp without the stamp is the non-holo copy in Trainer Deck A, which was never sold.

The stamped copies follow the starter set's printings: shadowless in the first, with the Unlimited design's drop shadow after that, and some with the ©1999-2000 copyright line of the last. The 2-Player CD-ROM Starter Set, sold alongside Base Set 2, held a copy in cosmos holofoil. Machamp is also missing from the cosmos holo test prints known of nearly every other Base Set holo, which CGC ties to its not being in regular packs.

description.text:
From the 2-Player Starter Set's second printing on, Machamp took the design of Base Set's Unlimited print, with a drop shadow around the picture and thicker HP and attack text, but kept its 1st Edition stamp. Most starter sets hold this copy, and collectors count it the commonest Base Set holo. They often call it the Unlimited Machamp, though every copy is stamped.

Its stamp is nearly always the thin one; collectors have seen only a handful with the thick stamp. Copies with a grayish stamp turn up too, more often on this card than on any other in one collector's experience.

The Machamp of the 2-Player Starter Set's first printing, in the shadowless design of Base Set's first print run: no drop shadow around the picture, thinner HP and attack text, and the 1st Edition stamp. Its stamp comes thick or thin, as on the other 1st Edition Base Set holos. Collectors call it the 1st Edition or the Shadowless Machamp, the same card: there is no shadowless holo Machamp without the stamp.

description.text:
Base Set Raichu with the green Prerelease stamp that Wizards of the Coast put on the Jungle Clefable, the prerelease promo of the original Pokémon League. The Clefables were stamped on uncut sheets that also held Base Set cards, Raichu among them, and on what was probably a test run the stamping machine stamped some Raichus along with the Clefables. The mistake was caught, and the stray Raichus went home with Wizards staff as keepsakes.

A Wizards manager showed one to a Media Factory employee at the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle in Hawaii, saying only 11 existed; another former employee, who owned one, recalled eight. The first photo was posted on PokeGym on April 1, 2006, so many took it for a joke. CGC certified two copies in 2023, both traced back to former Wizards employees, and the only PSA-graded copy is a PSA 6, auctioned by Heritage in September 2025.

description.text:
This copy is the yellow-cheeked shadowless Pikachu printed in Japan on Japanese card stock for the Pokémon Song Best Collection CD set, released in Japan on 1 January 1999, eight days before Base Set's first English release. It was the only English card among the set's eleven promos.

It has the English back and every feature of an ordinary shadowless Pikachu, so it is hard to tell apart: its colors are slightly lighter, and the thinner Japanese stock lets much more light through when you shine a torch behind it. Grading labels often don't distinguish it, so a copy in its original seal is the surest proof.
